paper.title: Logarithmic Regret for Online KL-Regularized Reinforcement Learning

unmapped: Objective is KL-regularized reward J(pi) = E[R*(x,a)] - (1/eta) KL(pi || pi_ref); regret measured against the KL-regularized optimal policy
Reference policy pi_ref and regularization parameter eta known to learner
Reward realizability in a finite function class R mapping to [0,1]; complexity via eluder dimension d(R, lambda, T)
Contexts drawn i.i.d. from d_0; noise is 1-sub-Gaussian zero mean
Access to a planning oracle computing the Gibbs policy
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t \ge 1$, the learner observes a context $x_t \in \cX$, and chooses an action $a_t \in \cA$ ... $r_t = R^*(x_t, a_t) + \epsilon_t$, where $R^*(x_t, a_t)$ is the unknown reward function and $\epsilon_t$ is an independent 1-sub-Gaussian zero-mean random noise. ... $J(\pi) := \rE_{x \sim d_0} \rE_{a \sim \pi(\cdot | x)} [R^*(x, a) - \frac{1}{\eta} \log \frac{\pi(a|x)}{\pi_{\reff}(a|x)}]$

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Episodic reinforcement learning (MDP with horizon H), not a bandit problem.
unmapped: KL-regularized value objective with reference policy pi_ref
Q-function class F with realizability and KL-regularized Bellman completeness
Bonus function class B with finite cardinality
settings.definition_quote: A Markov Decision Process (MDP) is defined by a tuple $\cM = (\cS, \cA, H, \PP, d_0, r)$ ... The objective is to find a policy $\pi$ that maximizes the following KL-regularized value: $J(\pi) = \E^{\pi} [\sum_{h = 1}^H r_h (s_h, a_h) - \eta^{-1} \sum_{h = 1}^H \log \frac{\pi_h(a_h|s_h)}{\pi_{\reff,h}(a_h|s_h)}]$

symbols.eta_KL: KL-regularization parameter eta (objective is R - (1/eta) KL)
symbols.N_R: cardinality of the reward function class R
symbols.d_R: eluder dimension d(R, lambda, T) of the reward class (Definition 3.3)

conditions: reward realizability: R* in a finite class R of functions into [0,1] (Assumption 3.2)

source.label: th:bandit
source.quote: Under Assumption \ref{as:Reward function realizability}, for any $\delta>0$, by taking $\beta_T=16\log(N_{\cR}T/\delta)$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the output of Algorithm \ref{alg:kl-bandits} satisfies $\mathrm{Regret}(T) = \cO\Big(\eta\log(N_{\cR}T/\delta)\cdot d(\cR,\lambda,T)\Big)$.

results.notes: Regret is sum_t J(pi*) - J(pi_t) of the KL-regularized objective (expected over contexts/actions per round), holding w.p. 1-delta. Relies on a planning oracle; compute not stated. Regret not formally defined in main text; definition from proof.

symbols.d_F: sum over h of eluder dimensions d(F_h, lambda, T)

conditions: bonus functions lie in a finite class B_h

source.label: th:mdp
source.quote: Under Algorithm \ref{alg:kl-mdp} and Assumptions \ref{as:Realizability} and \ref{as:Bellman completeness} with $\beta_h^T = \Theta(\sqrt{\log(N_h T H / \delta)})$, we have with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\mathrm{Regret}(T) = \cO\Big(\eta H^2 d(\cF,\lambda,T) \cdot \log(N_{\cF\oplus\cB} TH /\delta)\Big)$, where $d(\cF,\lambda,T)=\sum_{h=1}^Hd(\cF_h,\lambda,T)$ and $N_{\cF\oplus\cB}=\max_h N_{\cF_h}\cdot N_{\cF_{h+1}}\cdot N_{\cB_{h+1}}$.

results.notes: Out-of-scope episodic RL setting; T is the number of episodes.
